mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >25 bps in two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 5.0% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply chain weakness, which raises input costs and suppresses earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their prior 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a tight labor market that boosts wage growth and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average AND UNRATE falls by >0.2pp in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in housing starts (HOUST) below its 6-month moving average for three consecutive months signals weakening residential demand, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 6-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a concurrent decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1), signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces aggregate demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average AND GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
